stem: India's nationwide immunisation campaign, launched in 1995 to administer oral polio vaccine drops to all children under 5 years on designated National Immunisation Days, successfully making India polio-free by 2014, is called:
explanation: The Pulse Polio Programme's mass oral-vaccination drives on fixed National Immunisation Days eradicated wild poliovirus from India (certified polio-free in 2014) — distinct from the routine Universal Immunisation Programme (ongoing individual vaccination schedule) or Mission Indradhanush (targets unreached/under-immunised children for multiple vaccines).

stem: A virus that attacks and weakens the human immune system, spread through infected blood, unprotected sexual contact, or from mother to child, eventually leading (if untreated) to a condition where the body can no longer fight off common infections, is:

options.option_text: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), leading to AIDS

explanation: HIV progressively destroys immune cells; its advanced stage, AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome), leaves the body vulnerable to opportunistic infections — distinct from influenza (respiratory virus), Hepatitis A (typically food/water-borne, affects the liver), or rotavirus (a common cause of diarrhoea in children).
